references.text: Hebron is called here Kiriath-Arba, and Arba is described as the greatest among the Anakim, which connects to the description of Arba as 'the father of the Anakim'.
Caleb receives Kiriath-Arba (Hebron) and drives out the three sons of Anak from there, confirming Hebron's identification with Kiriath-Arba.
Hebron in the hill country of Judah is designated as one of the cities of refuge, the same city that is here given to the Levites.
Kiriath-Arba is identified with Hebron in the land of Canaan, where Sarah died and Abraham purchased a burial site.
Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre near Kiriath-Arba, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had lived.
The spies came to Hebron where the Anakim Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai lived, confirming Hebron's connection to the Anakim.
A parallel text in Chronicles describes how Aaron's descendants received Hebron in Judah along with its surrounding pasturelands.
